repositories.name: reviseloop

overview.tagline: Study Smarter. Revise Faster. An interactive, offline-friendly MCQ workspace for Computer Science exam preparation.
overview.description: A fast, zero-backend interactive MCQ practice, mock exam, and mistake-review platform built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, designed to run seamlessly both locally (file://) and on static hosts like GitHub Pages.
overview.problem_solved: Eliminates backend and CORS friction in Computer Science exam revision by providing an offline-capable, browser-based testing, mock exam, and mistake-tracking workspace.
overview.target_users: Computer Science students preparing for semester exams and technical assessments.

frameworks_and_libraries: Vanilla JavaScript (classic scripts, zero external runtime dependencies)

key_features: Dynamic URL-driven multi-subject loading (quiz.html?subject=<id>) via classic script injection without CORS errors
Isolated per-subject localStorage persistence for progress, missed answers, and bookmarked questions
In-browser custom .json and .js question bank uploader with schema validation, syntax checking, and downloadable starter templates

Five study and exam modes: Study Bank, Sequential Quiz (with option shuffling and undoable reset), Mock Exam (10/25/50/100 questions, Instant Feedback vs. Exam Mode), Missed/Wrong Review (auto-clearing on retry), and Saved Review
Automatic difficulty classification (Easy, Medium, Hard) based on computational/structural complexity when explicit tags are omitted
Structured explanation callouts normalizing exp, explanation, and feedback fields
Comprehensive keyboard shortcuts (N/J/Down, K/Up, A-D/1-4, T, S, E, /, [, ?, Esc) and mobile floating quick-nav dock
Responsive collapsible sidebar with live completion/accuracy telemetry and persistent Light/Dark theme switching

architecture.pattern: Zero-backend Multi-Page Application (MPA) with centralized global configuration (window.SITE_CONFIG) and dynamic script injection
folder_structure: quiz.html (Universal interactive quiz, mock exam & review workspace)
assets/css/global.css (Shared design tokens, typography, themes & ambient background)
assets/css/quiz.css (Sidebar, MCQ cards, modals & floating dock styles)
assets/js/config.js (Central site branding, links, catalog & quiz settings)
assets/js/subjects-data.js (Central subject registry with IDs, metadata, readiness & file paths)
assets/js/quiz-engine.js (Universal quiz engine, mock generator, upload validator & shortcuts)
assets/js/coming-soon.js (Dynamic metadata loader for unreleased subjects)
database_models_or_schema: Subject Registry Item: { id, title, semester, status, icon, description, ready, dataFile }
MCQ Question Item: { num, q, A, B, C, D, ans, exp, difficulty?, topic?, week? }

prerequisites: Any modern web browser (no build tools, server, or runtime dependencies required)
run_commands: Open index.html directly in a browser (file://) or host statically via GitHub Pages

challenges_solved: Eliminated browser file:// CORS issues without a bundler or server by using classic script injection and a global window.SITE_CONFIG registry
Prevented cross-course state collisions in browser storage via versioned, per-subject localStorage namespacing
Built heuristic auto-difficulty tagging to classify untagged MCQ banks into Easy, Medium, and Hard tiers
resume_bullets: Engineered a zero-backend, offline-compatible Computer Science MCQ and mock exam web platform using vanilla JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3, deployed on GitHub Pages.
Architected a dynamic script-injection loader and schema-validated local file uploader supporting custom .json and .js question banks without CORS dependencies.
Built five interactive study workflows—including timed mock exams, mistake-tracking review, keyboard-driven navigation, and isolated localStorage persistence—for multi-semester CS coursework.

repositories.name: mediai-care

overview.tagline: Enterprise Multi-Clinic & Telemedicine Platform with Calibrated Human-in-the-Loop AI Screening.
overview.description: A multi-clinic appointment, operations, and clinical decision-support healthcare platform built with Next.js 15 and PostgreSQL, extended with a FastAPI AI sidecar for explainable skin-lesion screening and RAG health assistance.
overview.problem_solved: Digitizes traditional medical center workflows—replacing manual phone bookings, walk-in queues, and fragmented doctor schedules—while enforcing strict multi-tenant data isolation and double-booking prevention at the database layer.
overview.target_users: Multi-branch clinics, clinic administrators, doctors, receptionists, and patients.

key_features: Multi-tenant SaaS architecture with strict database-level clinic isolation (clinicId scoping and appt_tenant_guard trigger)
Global patient identity portal allowing patients to manage visits across multiple clinics while keeping clinical records isolated

Database-level security guards (1_db_guards): partial unique index (uniq_active_slot) double-booking shield, immutable append-only AuditLog trigger, E.164 phone & email CHECK constraints, and Row-Level Security (RLS)

Hardened authentication supporting dual email/phone login, dummy-bcrypt timing-attack protection, brute-force account lockouts (5 failed attempts -> 15-min lock), and Edge middleware RBAC across 5 roles (SUPER_ADMIN, CLINIC_ADMIN, RECEPTIONIST, DOCTOR, PATIENT)
Dynamic booking slot engine, appointment state transitions, and responsive clinic/doctor dashboards
Deterministic multi-clinic database seeding (prisma/seed.ts) and automated SQL constraint attack verification suite (scripts/verify-db.ts)
Monorepo FastAPI AI service architecture designed for calibrated skin-lesion screening (Grad-CAM overlays, abstention gates) and vector-based RAG assistance

architecture.pattern: Full-Stack Monorepo (Next.js 15 App Router + FastAPI Python AI Sidecar) backed by Multi-Tenant PostgreSQL with DB-Level Triggers and RLS
folder_structure: ai-service/ (FastAPI Python AI microservice for skin-lesion screening and RAG)
prisma/migrations/1_db_guards/ (Custom SQL triggers, partial unique indexes, and CHECK constraints)
scripts/verify-db.ts (Automated database security guard verification runner)
src/app/api/health/ (System ping and DB connectivity health monitor)
src/types/next-auth.d.ts (Auth.js type augmentations for Role and ClinicId)
database_models_or_schema: 25-entity relational schema in prisma/schema.prisma (Users, Clinics, Doctors, Patients, Appointments, QueueCounters, AuditLogs)
SQL Guard: uniq_active_slot (partial unique index preventing overlapping active bookings)
SQL Guard: appt_tenant_guard (trigger rejecting cross-clinic doctor/patient appointment links)
SQL Guard: Append-only AuditLog trigger blocking UPDATE/DELETE operations

prerequisites: Managed Supabase PostgreSQL project or local Docker PostgreSQL instance

challenges_solved: Eliminated race-condition double-bookings and cross-tenant data leaks directly at the PostgreSQL engine level using partial unique indexes, triggers, and Row-Level Security
Mitigated credential-stuffing and timing-enumeration attacks via dummy bcrypt hashing, brute-force account lockouts, and Edge JWT middleware RBAC
Built an automated security verification harness (verify-db.ts) that simulates SQL constraint attacks against the database to guarantee invariant enforcement
resume_bullets: Architected a multi-tenant healthcare appointment and operations platform using Next.js 15, TypeScript, Prisma 6, and PostgreSQL (Supabase), deployed on Vercel.

Engineered database-level security invariants—including partial unique indexes for double-booking prevention, tenant-isolation triggers, immutable audit logs, and Row-Level Security—validated via an automated attack-simulation test suite.

Implemented Edge-enforced Role-Based Access Control (Auth.js v5) supporting 5 distinct clinical roles, dual email/E.164-phone authentication, brute-force lockouts, and a FastAPI sidecar architecture for human-in-the-loop AI skin-lesion screening.

repositories.name: plant-disease-diagnostic-system
repositories.category: AI / Computer Vision / AgriTech Web Application

overview.tagline: FloraScan AI — A dual-engine computer vision dashboard that classifies tomato leaf health in seconds, and refuses to guess when it is unsure.
overview.description: An end-to-end deep learning web application built with PyTorch and Streamlit for real-time tomato leaf disease diagnosis across five classes (Healthy, Bacterial Spot, Early Blight, Late Blight, and Not Leaf), featuring side-by-side model benchmarking, confidence abstention gates, and downloadable diagnostic reports.
overview.problem_solved: Provides rapid, accessible plant pathology diagnostics while preventing overconfident false-positive predictions on uncertain or non-leaf images via a 65% confidence safety threshold and synthetic out-of-distribution rejection.
overview.target_users: Farmers, agronomists, agricultural researchers, and home gardeners.

databases_and_storage: Git LFS & Hugging Face Hub (.pth model checkpoints)

key_features: Multi-engine inference switcher supporting Custom 3-Block CNN (96.53% test accuracy, 724/750) and ResNet-18 transfer learning (94.13% test accuracy, 706/750)
Dual Benchmark Mode running both models simultaneously on a single leaf image to compare agreement, disagreement, or uncertainty
Safety confidence threshold (65%) that flags low-confidence predictions as 'Unrecognized' instead of guessing
Out-of-distribution (OOD) rejection trained on a 1,000-image synthetic 'Not Leaf' class (noise, gradients, checkerboards, shapes)
Visual confidence gauge and 5-class probability distribution bars with a built-in Disease Library (symptoms, severity, and care plans)
Session scan history log, built-in sample leaf selector, and downloadable plain-text diagnosis reports
Cached inference with automatic model hot-reloading whenever .pth checkpoint files are updated

architecture.pattern: Modular Python/Streamlit ML Web Application with dual PyTorch inference engines and centralized configuration (config.py)
folder_structure: app.py (Streamlit interface: sidebar, tabs, and page flow)
config.py (Class labels, paths, 65% confidence threshold, UI metadata, and diagnostic guide)
model.py (PyTorch model builders, checkpoint loader, and cached inference)
ui.py (Custom HTML components: result cards, confidence gauge, probability bars, and report generator)
Plant_Disease_Detection_V2.ipynb (Data preprocessing, training, and evaluation notebook)
best_custom_cnn_5class.pth (Custom 3-Block CNN weights, 196 MB via Git LFS)
best_resnet18_5class.pth (ResNet-18 weights, 42.7 MB via Git LFS)
assets/ (UI screenshots and training/validation accuracy curves)
site/ (Static project landing page deployed on Vercel)
database_models_or_schema: Target Classes (ImageFolder order): ['Not_Leaf', 'Tomato_Bacterial_spot', 'Tomato_Early_blight', 'Tomato_Late_blight', 'Tomato_healthy']
CustomPlantCNN: 3x [Conv2d -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> MaxPool2d] + Dropout(0.25) -> Linear(100352->512) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> Dropout(0.25) -> Linear(512->5) (~51.5M trainable params)
ResNet-18 Baseline: Frozen ImageNet convolutional backbone + trainable Linear(512->5) classifier head (2,565 trainable params)

prerequisites: Git LFS (or manual download of .pth weights from Hugging Face Hub: asadalisajjad/FloraScan-AI-Weights)

challenges_solved: Prevented overconfident false diagnoses on ambiguous or non-leaf uploads by combining a 65% confidence abstention gate with a 1,000-image synthetic 'Not Leaf' OOD class

Built a side-by-side Dual Benchmark pipeline comparing a custom 3-block CNN (96.53% test accuracy) against a frozen ResNet-18 baseline (94.13% test accuracy) with cached execution and automatic checkpoint hot-reloading
Managed large PyTorch weight files (196 MB and 42.7 MB) cleanly using Git LFS with a Hugging Face Hub mirror and automated Streamlit uptime via GitHub Actions
resume_bullets: Developed FloraScan AI, an end-to-end computer vision web application built with PyTorch and Streamlit achieving 96.53% test accuracy across 5 tomato leaf health classes on a balanced 5,000-image PlantVillage dataset.

Engineered a dual-engine inference and benchmarking dashboard comparing a custom 3-block CNN against a transfer-learned ResNet-18 model, complete with a 65% confidence abstention threshold and synthetic out-of-distribution rejection.
Architected a modular, hot-reloadable ML inference pipeline with Git LFS and Hugging Face Hub weight distribution, downloadable diagnostic reports, and an accompanying Vercel showcase site.
